FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Electric Welding Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. In the preparation of this standard, assistance has been derived from the following: BS 635 : 1979 `Arc welding power sources, equipment accessories', issued by the British Standards Institution ( BSI ). IEC Dot: 26 (Central Office) 19-I-11 `Draft -Safety requirements for arc welding equipment Power sources', issued by the International Electrotechnical Commission ( IEC ). For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number of singnificant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

IS 13339 : 1992

Indian Standard

MULTIrOPERATORTYPEARCWELDING TRANSFORMERS- SPECIFICATION
1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard lays down the requirements of construction and methods of test for oil cooled three phase transformers of the flat characteristic type ( substantially constant voltage ) for manual multiple metal arc welding and associated current regulators. 1.2 This standarddoes not apply to conventional single/double operator transformers and transformer rectifier sets for manual multiple metal arc welding. 2 REFERENCES The following Indian Standards are necessary adjuncts to this standard: Is J~Q. Title Power transformers : Part 4 2026 ( Part 4 .) : 1977 T e r m i n a l m a r k i n g tappings and connections ( jirst reuislon ) 2834 : 1986 H801 : 191i8 Shunt capacitors for power systems ( second revision ) Plugs, sockets and terminal arrangements for manual arc welding equipment 3.4 Rating A statement of limitation of performance parameter under specified operating conditions assigned by the manufacturer 3.5 Open Circuit Voltage The output voltage exclusive of any arc stabilizing, or arc striking voltage across the neutral and any phase ot the transformer ready to weld but carrying no wtlding current. 3.6 Rating Welding Current a) The ma.ximum continuous hand welding (.urr ent for regulators, and b; The continuous test current for the power source. 3.7 Maximum Continuous Hand Welding Current The minimum current which may be drawn through the current regulator at the conventional load voltage and at the rated duty cycle without exceeding the stated temperature rise. 3.8 Maximum Hand Welding Current The maximum current obtainable through the regulator at the conventional load voltage. 3.9 Minimum Hand Welding Current The minimum current obtainable through the regulator at the conventional load voltage. 3.10 Conventional Load Voltage The voltage measured between the output terminal of the regulator and the `work' return terminal ( Neutral ) of the transformer when a specified current is flowing through a conventional load. 3.10.1 The conventional load voltage for metal arc welding is given in Table 1. 3.11 Conventiotial Load A practically non-inductive resistive load having a power factor of 0.99 or more. 3.12 Continuous Test Current Current to be drawn continuously from the power source or through the regulator when being tested for temperature rise.

3

TERMINOLOGY

3.0 For the purpose of this standard, the following definitions shall apply. 3.1 Manual Metal Arc Welding ( Hand Welding ) Metal arc welding with consumable electrodes not exceeding 460 mm in length and applied by the operator without automatic or semi-automatic means of replacement. 3.2 Multiple Metal Arc Welding Power Source A power source capable of supplying current simultaneously to three or more operators through suitable regulator engaged in manual metal arc welding without objectionabie arc interactions. 3.3 Duty Cycle The ratio of time during. which the regulator on the output side of' the >ower source is-loaded to the total time of a complete cycle expressed in percentage. In this standard, the cycle duration 1s 5 minutes.

The current regulators shall be suitable for use i n conjunction with a power source having rated open circuit voltage of 90 V. 4.2.2 Rated Welding Current The rated welding current of the regulator shall be the maximum continuous hand welding current. 4.2.2.1 .Tbere will be four sizes of current regulators having the rated current as under: 210 A, 350 A, 450 A and 600 A 4.2.3 Number of Operator per Phase The number of operators per phase of different sizes of transformers are given in Table 5. The rated duty cycle at maximum continuous hand welding current shall be 60 percent. A complete cycle consists of 3 minutes of load period fol!o\\ed by 2 minutes of no load operation. 6 DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION 6.1 Transformer Power Source 6.1.1 The transformer power source shall be of substantially flat characteristic. The regulation ( the difference between the no load secondary voltage and the secondary voltage ) at rated current and 0.35 p f. lagging shall not exceed 3 percent of the no load secondary voltage. 6.1.2 The power source shall be double wound and the secondary or the output terminals shall be insulated from the tank. The terminals shall be marked in accordance with IS 2026 ( Part 4 ) : 1977. 6.1.3 Earthing Two earthing terminals of at least 50 mms section, each shall be provided where all metal parts of the equipment likely to become charged accidentally, shall be connected. The earthing terminals shall be protected against corrosion and shall be indelibly marked with the following symbol

4.2.4 Maximum Hand MJelding Current The maximum hand welding current shall be the same as the rated current of the regulator. 4.2.5 Minimum Hand Welding Current The minimum hand welding current shall be not more than 20 percent of the rated current. 4.3 Limits of Temperature Rise The maximum temperature rise shall be as shown in Table 6. 3 6.1.3.1 These terminals shall not be used for any other purpose ( such as clamping two parts of the casing together ). 6.1.4 The following are the general requirements of the power source: a) Enclosure or the tank shall be suitable for outdoor operation; b) The secondary and the neutral shall be insulated from the tank;

Suitable means for anchoring both the incoming and outgoing cables shall be provided; Output terminals shall be suitably shrouded to avoid accidental or inadvertent contact; Primary terminals shall be suitably covered so that these are not accessible to unauthorised persons; An oil conservator shall not be provided; A thermometer pocket shall be provided; Provision shall be made so that oil level may be checked easily; Lifting hooks or suitable provisions for lifting shall be provided; Output terminals shall be of the busbar type and suitable for bolts as indicated in Table 7; The output terminals shall be suitable for accommodating cable sockets equal in number to the number of 350 A operators per phase plus one per phase on three operator transformers and two per phase on six, nine and twelve operator transformers so that additional distribution boxes may be fed at reduced currents, if required; and

6.2.5 The enclosure or the tank shall be suitable for outdoor operation. 6.2.6 Provision for earthing shall be made as in 6.1.3. 6.2.7 Wheels shall not be provided. 6.2.8 Provision shall be made for lifting the regulator. 6.2.9 Oil drain plug shall be provided. 6.2.10 Provision shall be made so that oil level may be checked easily. 7 POWER FACTOR CORRECTION CAPACITORS 7.1 A capdclcor may be used to improve the power factor to approximately U.85 lagging at 30 percent 01 the rated welding current 01 the power source. 7.2 The capacitor, if used, shall be so connected that it is swltched off witn the transformer. 7.3 `l`he capacitor, of used, shall conform to 1 3 2834 : 1986. 7.4 The ratmg in KVar of the capacitor to be used with dlttelrllt sizes of the transfbrmer power source shall be 111 accordance wlrh l'able 8. 6.2 Series Current Regulators 6.2.1 In case when output current is controlled by means of tappings, the number of current setting positions in the range shall be not less than 30. 6.2.2 Provisions Shall be made for visual indication of the output current setting in amperes. 6.2.3 The series current regulator shall be provided with terminals in accordance with IS 8804 : 1978. Sockets shall not be used. 6.2.4 The terminals shall be suitably shrouded to avoid accidental or inadvertent contact. 4

The measuring device used shall not interfere with the normal ventilation of the welding power source or the regulator or cause of transfer of heat to or from it.

IS 13339 : 1992 8.1.4 The accuracy of measuring instrument shall be as under: Class 1-O a) Electrical measuring instrument f 0 5�C b) Thermometers c) Thermocouples or resistance thermometers a) Type tests, and b) Routine tests. 8.2 Type Tests They shall be made on one power source or regulator of each type or design or size to show that it complies with all the requirements of this standard. The records of type tests on a power source or a regulator which in essential details is representative of the one being purchased, produced by the manufacturer shall be accepted by the purchaser or his representative as evidence of type test instead of actual test. The presence of the purchaser or his representative during the tests shall be a matter of special agreement between the purchaser and manufacturer . 8.2.1 Trantformer Powtr Source Type tests and their sequence shall be as follows: resistance a) Insulation test ( see 8.4 ), preliminary check, b) Open circuit voltage test ( see 8.5 ), c) Temperature rise test ( see 8.6 ), d) Test for voltage regulation ( see 8.8 ), e) High voltage test ( see 8.7 ), and f 0.5% to all the tests listed under `Routine Test'. 8.6.10.!2 The test shall be regarded as completed. when the top oil temperature rise does not vary by more than l�C per hour during four consecutive hourly seadings. 8.6.11 Temperahsre Correction jGr Equipment After Shut Down Coding of the

If the winding temperature is measured by taking resistance method after the shut down of the equipment a suitable correction shall be applied

IS 13339 : 1992 so as to obtain as nearly as practicable the temperature of the winding at the instant of turning off the power. For this purpose, the hot resistance reading and the time from shut down to measurement shall be recorded. 8.6.11.1 Correction factors If the load loss in the winding does not exceed 8 watts per kg of copper or 2.5 watts per kg of aluminium no correction is necessary if the measurement is done within 2 minutes after shut down. But if the measurement is done after 2 minutes then correction shall be made according to 8.6.11.2. 8.6.11.2 If the load loss in the winding exceed 8 watts per kg of copper or 2.5 watts per kg of aluminium but does not exceed 66 W per kg of copper: or 20 W per kg of aluminium the correct i o n i n d e g r e e s celsms ( to be added to the measured ) temperature shall be the product of the loss in watts per kg of the conductor multiplied by the correction factor given in Table 9. .8.6.12 Testing Methods At the choice of the manufacturer, any one of the following methods shall be used for transformers: a) Short circuit method ( 8.6.13 ), b) Back to back method ( 8.6.14 ), and c) Direct loading on an external adjustable resistance reactance ( 8.6.15 ), and for regulators ( 8.6.16 ). .8.6.13 Short Circuit Method of Trmperature R i s e Test In this method, the total losses ( taken as the sum of the measured load loss at rated current corrected to 75�C and the measured no load loss ) are
TEMPRATURE RISE

supplied to the transformer windings. This condition is maintained for a period indicated in 8.6.10. At the end of this period, the top oil temperature is recorded. The input power is then reduced to a value which results in the circulation of rated current at rated frequency in the windings and this value is maintained for 1 hour. The top oil temperature and the resistance of the windings are then recorded again. The temperature rise of the windings shall be taken as the sum of the temperature rise of windings, calculated from resistance measurement plus the difference between the first and second top oil temperature. 8.6.14 Back to Back Method

of

Temperature Rise

In this method, rated currents and rated exciting voltages are applied to the transformer under test. The test is continued in terms of 8.6.10, the final oil temperature and the resistance of the windings are recorded. The temperature rise of windings are calculated from the measured values. 8.6.15 Direct Loading Method of Temperature Rise Test In this method, rated load is applied to the transformer windings and the test is continued for a period indicated in 8.6.10. The oil temperature and resistance of windings are recorded. 8.6.16 Temperature Rise `Test of Regulator The regulator shall be set at its maximum current setting. A continuous test current is passed through the regulator for a period indicated in 8.6.10 at the end of which oil temperature and resistance of winding shall be recorded. The temperature rise of oil and winding is calculated from these recorded values, The continuous test current shall be the rated current multiplied by 0.6.

8.7.1 The high voltage test shall be applied once only on a new and completely assembled power source or a regulator. The insulation shall withstand the test voltage without any flashover or breakdown.

Standard Mark The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for, the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
